amendments.body: Blocker: this patch does not implement bead `tanksim-6e5.7.2`. The substantive changes are all alkalinity-budget plumbing in `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:12-23`, `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:366-384`, `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/systems/water_change.rs:99-153`, and `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:67-123`. None of the task’s priority parameter families are annotated with provenance/confidence metadata, and no developer-facing provenance summary/doc was added, so the acceptance criteria for 6e5.7.2 remain unimplemented.
amendments.rationale: The branch appears to be solving a different bead entirely; merging it for 6e5.7.2 would leave the requested provenance work undone.

amendments.body: Significant maintainability risk: the new alkalinity accounting stores meq values in APIs and fields that are explicitly named as mg, including `ElementBudget.in_mg/out_mg/net_mg` in `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:35-56`, the alkalinity field docs in `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:72-76`, the concrete assignment in `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/systems/water_change.rs:149-152`, and the helper/assertion surface in `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:64-83` plus `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:418-507`. This removes unit safety from the type system and makes it easy for later callers to mix mg and meq tolerances or diagnostics without the compiler catching it.
amendments.rationale: This is not just naming polish: the patch now relies on one generic budget type to represent different physical units, which is the kind of ambiguity that produces future accounting/debugging mistakes.

payload.summary: Reviewed the patch end-to-end and found one blocker plus one API-level maintainability risk. Targeted touched-area tests passed. `cargo test -p tank_core` still fails in `save_load_with_active_cycle_state`, but that failure reproduces on `HEAD~1`, so I treated it as pre-existing rather than introduced by this diff.
